Title: June 25, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting
Overview: Council deliberated on the major update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, straw-polling conditions of approval and recommended amendments from the Planning Board, County Planning Commission, and Board of County Commissioners, then approved the plan with those changes by unanimous motions, though it still needs further rounds of approval by the other bodies. Council also gave staff direction to develop a $400 million recreation and public safety bond and a vacancy excise tax for the November 2026 ballot, and heard results from the Fund Our Future community engagement.

Topic1.Title: Staff overview of the plan approval process
Topic1.Summary: Planning staff explained that the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan must be adopted in identical form by all four approving bodies, so this meeting was deliberation only with no public testimony. Staff outlined a series of motions and a likely second round of consideration in July and August. Staff noted the Planning Board and Board of County Commissioners conditions of approval are binding unless council agrees to them.

Topic2.Title: Conditions of approval from Planning Board and County Commissioners
Topic2.Summary: Planning Board conditioned approval on changes to housing policy 82 and the municipal airport policy 79. The Board of County Commissioners proposed six conditions, including tribal consultation language, deleting four pages of planning history, and changing area two neighborhood one designations to rural. Staff recommended against most conditions but supported some language edits, and noted the county changes would need further review.

Topic3.Title: Recommended amendments from the four approval bodies
Topic3.Summary: Staff reviewed 14 recommended amendments, including adding residential uses to the industrial designation, changing street and parks language, and redesignating several East Boulder parcels to Innovation and Production Hub or industrial. Staff opposed most map changes as inconsistent with the East Boulder Subcommunity Plan and unreviewed by the community. Staff supported several smaller edits, including county renewable energy and rural working lands language.

Topic4.Title: Council clarifying questions and deliberation
Topic4.Summary: Council asked whether middle-income housing and attainable housing were adequately addressed, and whether affordability language could be used to limit housing near the airport. Staff explained that the policy emphasizes middle-income housing under policy 84 and that the airport lists are examples rather than mandates. Council members also questioned the removal of the planning history section and the climate and water priorities in the plan.

Topic5.Title: Straw poll on housing diversity and supply (policy 82)
Topic5.Summary: Council considered whether to keep the original policy 82 language or adopt Planning Board or County Commissioner edits that would emphasize more affordable housing and prioritize middle housing. Several members argued the county language was valuable because the county controls land that could be housed, but the mayor noted its rural proposal would discourage county housing. After successive straw polls, council kept the original language.

Topic6.Title: Straw poll on municipal airport language (policy 79)
Topic6.Summary: Council debated Planning Board revisions to the airport policy, which added noise management examples and ongoing county coordination. Matt Benjamin proposed a middle-ground version, but council members were split on whether the language was operational or aspirational. Following straw polls, council retained the original airport policy language.

Topic7.Title: Board of County Commissioners conditions straw polls
Topic7.Summary: Council accepted county conditions to add county references and remove American Indian from policy 102, and to remove the word city from policy 103 to limit it to city action. Council rejected the proposal to delete the 50-year planning history pages after discussion about accuracy and the potential to revise later. Council also agreed to add federally before recognized tribes in a related policy, and voted to change only the Gunbarrel area two neighborhood one designations to rural rather than all of area two.

Topic8.Title: Straw polls on recommended amendments
Topic8.Summary: Council straw polled staff and board recommended amendments one by one, asking first whether any member would advocate each change. Council approved Planning Board edits to the housing and transportation definitions, the parks and streets language, and the small houses on small lots language with multi-unit buildings near transit. Council rejected the 15-minute neighborhood monitoring language as operational and removed the proposed industrial residential map changes after straw polls.

Topic9.Title: Wildfire life safety and renewable energy amendments
Topic9.Summary: Council Member Kaplan proposed adding language requiring a holistic wildfire risk approach, including emergency management and egress capacity, when evaluating density within mapped wildfire ignition zones. Staff suggested it could fit better as an example in the natural hazards section, and council adopted it as a recommendation. Council also approved adding renewable before energy in local energy generation policy 53 and accepted the county's emergency utility services language in policy 16.

Topic10.Title: Motions to approve the comprehensive plan
Topic10.Summary: Council adopted four motions to approve the major update, approving the plan with the Board of County Commissioners conditions, the recommended amendments, and council conditions, all as indicated by the straw polls. Each motion passed unanimously on roll call. The mayor noted the process is not complete because the other approval bodies must still act.

Topic11.Title: Ballot measure direction for city facilities
Topic11.Summary: Staff presented polling results showing that a $400 million recreation and safety bond polled better than a $200 million option, though neither reached a majority on its own. Council agreed by a show of hands to pursue a tax ballot measure focused on city facilities and to advance the $400 million bond for future public hearings. Some members expressed concern about rising costs, the need for spending discipline, and the risk of failure at the ballot.

Topic12.Title: Vacancy excise tax ballot measure direction
Topic12.Summary: Pollster Adam Probolsky reported that a vacancy tax on second and third homes had strong majority support, with about 70 percent more likely to vote yes after learning the details. Council members said the tax should target non-occupied second homes rather than rentals that are actively marketed. Council voted seven in favor to move the vacancy excise tax ballot measure forward for further consideration.

Topic13.Title: Fund Our Future community engagement results
Topic13.Summary: Consultant Micah Intermill and budget analyst Stacy Polleycove presented results from Fund Our Future, which reached 599 residents through community conversations and an online survey. Wildfire response and prevention emerged as the strongest priority for renters and homeowners, with operational maintenance also widely supported. Renters strongly prioritized affordable housing while homeowners ranked it near the bottom, and the results will inform the 2027 budget and the long-term financial plan due in November.
